Thanks Cara — following up from our demo last week. As discussed, attached is a concise MAP section focused on performance benchmarking for the Streamline pilot so we can unblock procurement and target the May 28 close.

High-level scope
- Objective: validate that Redwood meets Streamline's production SLOs for conversation latency and concurrent throughput for the pilot workload.
- Deliverables: benchmark report (p50/p95 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec throughput), test artifacts, run logs, and a signed acceptance email.

Proposed workload definition (see attached streamline_workload_profile.csv)
- Traffic mix: 60% short chat (avg 30 tokens), 30% medium prompts (avg 120 tokens), 10% long-form (avg 800 tokens).
- Tokenization: BPE / UTF-8; typical generation length capped to 1024 tokens.
- Key scenarios: cold-start first-token-time (TTFT), steady-state throughput at fixed concurrency, and cold vs warm cache runs.

Success criteria / SLOs
- TTFT (first-token): p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 450ms
- Latency (generation end): p50 <= 300ms (short), p95 <= 900ms (short)
- Throughput: sustained 1200 tokens/sec across 100 concurrent sessions
- Concurrency test: maintain latency SLOs at up to 250 concurrent sessions with degraded-acceptable fallback to smaller model

Acceptance tests
1) Baseline: single-session TTFT matrix (3 runs) — pass if SLO met
2) Ramp: increase concurrency in steps (10, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250) observing p95
3) Stress: 1-hour sustained run at target peak load with KV cache enabled

Timing and owners
- Baseline & ramp runs: May 20 (Marissa / Sergio)
- Stress & final acceptance: May 21 (Marissa)
- Report and artifact delivery: May 21 end of day

Attachments referenced:
- streamline_workload_profile.csv (CSV attachment — workload scenarios)

Next actions
- Please confirm the concurrency targets above and your procurement deadline. If that looks good we'll lock the kickoff for May 20 10:00AM PT and I will share the runbook.

Thanks,

Adding the engineering plan and concrete test matrix so everyone has visibility. I own the runs; Sergio will monitor infra; Rishi will validate cost/allocation and fallbacks.

Benchmark runbook (attached: benchmark_runbook.md) — highlights
- Test environments: dedicated pilot pool (g4dn-equivalent), model variant: redwood-open-1.2 (FP16) and redwood-open-1.2-q4 (quantized) for fallback.
- Measurement windows: warm-cache (after 5 warmup runs) and cold-cache (fresh VM, empty KV).
- Metrics captured: TTFT (ms), completion latency (ms), tokens/sec, GPU utilization (%), memory pressure, 95/99th tail jitter.

Test matrix (attached: test_matrix.xlsx) — example rows
- Scenario A (short chat): concurrency steps [1,10,25,50,100,150,200]; generation length 30 tokens; 3 repeats per step
- Scenario B (mixed prompts): concurrency steps [10,25,50,100]; avg 120 tokens
- Scenario C (long form): concurrency steps [1,5,10,25]; avg 800 tokens; prioritized for p95 tracking

Pass/fail logic
- A test step passes if p95 latency <= target SLO and no error rate > 0.5% for token generation failures.
- Final acceptance requires all critical scenario steps to pass and for throughput decline between warm/cold runs to be within 20%.

Artifacts delivered after runs:
- test_results_summary_20260520.pdf (summary + plots)
- raw logs (S3 link in delivery note)

Operational notes
- We'll use continuous batching tuned to the short-chat distribution; batching window 6ms for steady-state.
- KV cache prefixing will be enabled for medium/long scenarios to mirror expected app behavior.

Proposed schedule
- May 20 10:00AM PT: kickoff & baseline runs
- May 20 14:00–18:00 PT: ramp & stress runs
- May 21: report assembly and delivery

If you confirm the concurrency numbers Cara mentioned (peak 220), we'll add an extra ramp step at 220.
